prompts.text: What's a first impression of someone that changed after you got to know them?
Tell us about meeting a friend in an unlikely place.
Get to know someone through shared work or through a relaxed conversation?
A new colleague joins a team where everyone already knows one another. What's a useful first invitation?
People reveal different sides of themselves depending on the setting.
Being shy at a first meeting says little about someone's interest in other people.
What helps you remember a new person's name after an introduction?
Describe a stranger who gave you helpful advice in a brief conversation.
Several people know each other only online and arrange their first meeting. What would help everyone feel at ease?
Which friendship began with an unexpectedly ordinary conversation?
How has your idea of a dependable friend changed over time?
Friends who share your interests or friends who challenge your thinking?
Tell us about reconnecting with someone after years of little contact.
One friend changes their routine after starting a new job. How should the group adjust expectations?
Long friendships often survive changes because people allow one another to evolve.
A friendship doesn't need constant updates to remain meaningful.
What makes a reunion feel comfortable rather than awkward?
Recall an old acquaintance who remembered something kind about you.
You hear that a former classmate is visiting the area. What would make you reach out?
Meet old friends in a familiar place or choose somewhere new together?
What's a small sign that someone respects your time?
Tell us about a time a person handled a delay with unusual consideration.
Arrive early and settle in or arrive exactly when the gathering begins?
A group activity runs longer than planned and someone needs to leave. How should the others respond?
People's schedules reveal very little about how much they care for their friends.
Saying how long you have available is better than agreeing to plans you can't keep.
Which invitation makes it easiest for you to decide whether to attend?
Describe an occasion when changing a meeting time made everyone more comfortable.
Friends disagree about how far they should travel to meet. What would be a fair arrangement?
What makes you feel welcome when you arrive later than everyone else?
What's one thing a group should do when planning around different personalities?
Take turns leading a group project or divide roles according to strengths?
Tell us about a team where someone quiet made a crucial contribution.
A group assignment has no clear organiser. How would you help it get started?
Some people lead through preparation, while others shine during unexpected challenges.
A group succeeds more easily when people respect different working styles.
What task do friends tend to ask you to handle because they know your strengths?
Recall finishing a shared project and feeling proud of the way everyone contributed.
Two friends volunteer for the same role and neither wants to step aside. How should the team decide?
Work side by side on a challenge or divide it into independent parts?
What's the most useful response when a friend asks for your opinion about a personal choice?
Tell us about advice you received from a peer that stayed with you.
Offer an immediate reaction or ask a few questions before giving your view?
Someone tells the group about a decision they're unsure of. How would you avoid making it feel like a vote?
People sometimes ask friends for reassurance when they already know their preferred choice.
Respecting a friend's decision includes accepting when they don't follow your advice.
When do you prefer encouragement over detailed feedback?
Recall giving someone advice and later learning that they chose another path.
A friend wants honest feedback on something they're proud of. What's a considerate way to begin?
Which phrases help you feel heard during a difficult conversation?
What makes somebody feel safe sharing a personal story with a group?
Keep personal updates brief or share one longer story when everyone has time?
Describe a moment when your group protected someone's confidence.
Someone starts telling a story about another friend who isn't present. How would you check whether it's appropriate to share?
A good listener notices when a person hesitates before giving more detail.
Being close to someone doesn't give you ownership of their private experiences.
How do you signal that a topic is too personal for a particular setting?
Tell us about a time a friend respected a boundary without asking for an explanation.
A group photograph includes someone who doesn't want it posted online. What's the right next step?
Ask permission before taking photos or take them freely but ask before sharing?
Which quality helps friendships recover after a disagreement?
Recall a time a group changed plans after hearing a concern they'd overlooked.
Address tension before the next gathering or find a quiet moment during it?
Two friends disagree over a shared expense after an outing. What information would help settle it fairly?
People often need different amounts of time before they feel ready to revisit conflict.
Resolving a disagreement doesn't require everyone to pretend they saw it the same way.
What does a sincere effort to rebuild trust look like among friends?
Tell us about an apology that restored a friendship over time.
A friend admits they repeated something private. How should the group respond while protecting the person affected?
When is it better to ask a neutral friend to help with a conversation?
What's a social rule you grew up with that surprises people from other backgrounds?
Let everyone bring a dish to a gathering or have one person plan the whole meal?
Tell us about learning a useful custom from a friend with a different upbringing.
A group hosts visitors from several cultures and wants everyone to feel respected. What would you ask in advance?
People express respect through different habits, including silence, eye contact and greetings.
Curiosity about a custom is welcome when it leaves the other person free to decline an explanation.
Which local tradition would you enjoy explaining to a new friend?
Describe a celebration where you learnt why a custom mattered to the people practising it.
Two friends have different expectations about bringing gifts when visiting. How might they discuss it comfortably?
Learn a new greeting from everyone or exchange favourite sayings from home?
What shared experience makes an ordinary group gathering feel memorable?
Tell us about the first time your friends tried an activity none of you knew how to do.
A low-pressure picnic or a casual visit to a free local event?
The group arrives at a venue and finds it unexpectedly closed. How would you choose a backup plan?
An outing sometimes improves when everyone agrees to change expectations.
The best group plans leave room for people who enjoy different levels of activity.
Which outdoor activity works well for friends with different energy levels?
Recall an unplanned detour that turned into the highlight of a day with friends.
One friend wants to stay out late and another has an early morning. What would be a respectful way to split plans?
Which inexpensive outing would you recommend to a group visiting your city?
What do you hope people feel after spending time with your group?
Make a shared scrapbook or collect short voice memories from each person?
Tell us about the first gathering when a collection of acquaintances began to feel like friends.
A friend has to miss an important get-together. What's a thoughtful way to include them afterwards?
Group friendships often form around the small things people repeatedly choose to do together.
Good groups create space for changing interests without making anyone feel left behind.
What new tradition would suit friends who rarely have time to meet?
Recall an occasion when your group welcomed someone who later became a close friend.
Your group decides to invite one new person to the next outing. What would make their first hour comfortable?
End a meet-up with everyone sharing one highlight or let the evening end naturally?
